claims.text: Low-pain options (tretinoin, tazarotene, cantharidin) are used first, especially in children.
claims.quote: Treatments that cause minimal pain (eg, tretinoin, tazarotene, cantharidin) used first, especially in children.

claims.text: Other options: trichloroacetic acid 25 to 40%, podofilox in adults
claims.quote: Options include curettage, cryosurgery, laser therapy, electrocautery, trichloroacetic acid (25 to 40% solution), cantharidin, podophyllotoxin (podofilox) in adults, berdazimer, tretinoin, and tazarotene.

claims.text: Cantharidin: one small drop per lesion; washed off with soap and water in 6 to 24 hours; fewer than 15 lesions a session; not on the face or near the eyes (can scar the cornea); warn parents about blistering
claims.quote: It is applied in 1 small drop directly to the molluscum lesion. Areas that patients (especially children) may rub are covered with a bandage because contact with the fingers should be avoided. Cantharidin should not be applied to the face or near the eyes because blistering is unpredictable. If cantharidin comes into contact with the cornea, it can cause scarring. Cantharidin should be washed off with soap and water in 6 to 24 hours. Fewer than 15 lesions should be treated in one session because infection may occur after application of cantharidin. Parents should be warned about blistering if their children are prescribed this irritant.

claims.text: Berdazimer 10.3% gel (age 1 and older): once daily at home for up to 12 weeks, not on mucous membranes; cleared all lesions in over one-third of patients in trials
claims.quote: Berdazimer 10.3% gel is a topical agent available for use in patients 1 year and older that has demonstrated favorable efficacy (ie, clearing all molluscum lesions in over one-third of patients) and safety in randomized trials (1). It is applied at home once daily to the lesion (may not be used over mucous membranes) for up to 12 weeks.
